Source format: maintenance manual

- MV – Marlowe Viaduct
- HSA – Highways and Structures Agency
- PI – Principal Inspection
- GI – General Inspection
- SI – Special Inspection
- NDT – Non-destructive testing
- SWS – Safe Work Statement
- PT – Post-tensioning

2. Inspection Regimes

2.1 General Inspection (GI)

A General Inspection shall be carried out at intervals not exceeding twelve months. The inspection shall be a visual examination of all parts of the structure that are readily accessible without special access equipment. The inspecting engineer shall record all defects, deterioration, and any changes from the previous inspection.

2.2 Principal Inspection (PI)

A Principal Inspection shall be carried out at intervals not exceeding six years. The PI shall involve close examination of all parts of the structure, including those requiring special access arrangements, such as the underside of the deck, the bearings, and the PT anchorages.

2.3 Special Inspections (SI)

Special Inspections shall be carried out following any exceptional event, including:
- Major flood events
- Vehicle impact on the structure or parapets
- Fire beneath or on the structure
- Seismic events (however minor)
- Any report of unusual vibration or movement

2.4 Inspection Schedule

| Inspection Type | Frequency | Responsible Party | Notes |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------------|-------|
| Routine visual | Monthly | HSA Area Crew | Drives over structure; check parapets, deck surface, drainage |
| GI | Annual | HSA Structures Team | Full visual from ground level and deck |
| PI | 6-yearly | HSA Structures Team / Specialist | Includes access units, PT inspection |
| SI | As required | HSA Structures Team | Triggered by events or findings |

In the Marlowe Viaduct Maintenance Manual 2019, the construction start date is recorded as 1968-04-15. Record status: historical.

3. Inspection Checklists

3.1 Monthly Routine Checklist

| Item | Check | Acceptance Criteria | Action if Failed |
|------|-------|---------------------|------------------|
| Deck surface | Potholes, rutting, debris | No defects > 20 mm deep | Arrange repair; clean deck |
| Expansion joints | Condition, debris, water tightness | Joints clear, no leakage | Clean or repair as required |
| Parapet/barriers | Impact damage, corrosion, loose fixings | No damage, fixings secure | Report to structures team |
| Drainage outlets | Blockage, standing water | Free-flowing | Clear blockage |
| Bearings (where visible) | Displacement, corrosion, debris | No visible distress | Report to structures team |
| Soffit (from ground) | Cracks, staining, spalling | No new or propagating cracks | Report to structures team |

3.2 General Inspection Checklist (Abridged)

| Item | Check | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| Deck | Cracking, spalling, delamination | Record on defect sheet |
| Parapets | Alignment, corrosion, fixings | Check all posts and rails |
| Bearings | Movement, corrosion, rubber condition | Record any anomalies |
| Piers/abutments | Cracks, leaching, vegetation | Check for settlement or scour |
| River protection | Scour, undermining | Record water level at time |
| Approach embankments | Erosion, settlement | Check for voids |

4. Maintenance Procedures

4.1 Concrete Repairs

4.1.1 Assessment

Before any concrete repair, the extent of the defect shall be assessed and recorded. Delaminated areas shall be identified by hammer tapping. The area shall be marked out and the extent of repair agreed with the structures team.

2. Inspection Regime and Frequencies
3. Inspection Checklists

6. Drainage and Water Management

Appendix A – Defect Report Form
Appendix B – Lubrication Record Sheet

5. Lubrication Schedule

5.1 General

Lubrication shall be carried out in accordance with the intervals given below. All work shall be recorded on the Lubrication Record Sheet (Appendix B). Only lubricants specified by the bearing or equipment manufacturer shall be used. Where a grease nipple is missing or damaged, the item shall be reported and made good before the next lubrication visit.

The viaduct has three bearing types in service:

- Type A – Pot bearings (piers P2, P3, P4)
- Type B – Roller bearings (abutment A1)
- Type C – Elastomeric bearings (abutment A2, pier P1)

Note: Type B bearings at abutment A1 were replaced during the 2017 strengthening works. The original 1968 installation had a different lubrication point arrangement; refer to the as-built drawings for the current configuration.

5.2 Lubrication Intervals

| Item | Location | Interval | Lubricant | Notes |
|------|----------|----------|-----------|-------|
| Bearing pots – Type A | Piers P2, P3, P4 | 12-monthly | Grease, lithium-based NLGI 2 | Remove old grease before re-greasing |
| Bearing rollers – Type B | Abutment A1 | 6-monthly | Grease, molybdenum disulphide NLGI 2 | Check for free movement before greasing |
| Elastomeric bearings – Type C | Abutment A2, Pier P1 | No lubrication required | – | Inspect for cracking or bulging |
| Expansion joint – deck level | All joints | 6-monthly | Silicone spray | Apply sparingly; avoid overspray on deck |
| Drainage gulley gratings | Deck outlets | 12-monthly | Penetrating oil | Only if stiff or corroded |
| Access ladder hinges | Piers P2, P3 | Annually | General-purpose oil | Check fixings at same time |
| Parapet post base plates | All posts | 24-monthly | Wax-based rust preventative | Apply after cleaning |
The top and bottom plates shall be checked for distortion, and the anchorage bolts tested for
tightness using a torque wrench set to the values given on the as-built drawings. Where bolts
have been replaced, the replacement grade and torque shall be noted on the inspection record.

6.3 Roller Bearings (Type B)

Roller bearings at abutment A1 are of the multi-roller type. Free movement shall be confirmed
by observing the displacement of the bearing relative to the sole plate during a thermal
cycle, where practicable. The rollers shall be checked for pitting, rusting or flat spots.
Where any roller shows surface corrosion, the bearing shall be reported and a programme of
cleaning and re-greasing arranged.

Note: The replacement bearings installed in 2017 are fitted with a sealed cover plate.
Lubrication is via the two nipples on the side face. Do not attempt to open the cover plate
during routine inspection; this shall only be done during major works.

6.4 Elastomeric Bearings (Type C)

Elastomeric bearings at abutment A2 and pier P1 shall be visually checked for:

- Splitting or cracking of the rubber surface
- Bulging at the edges
- Uneven deformation suggesting overloading
- Displacement from the bearing shelf

Where bulging is observed, the bearing shall be checked for rebound after unloading. Any
permanent set shall be recorded and the bearing monitored at three-monthly intervals until
the next full structural assessment.

7. Concrete Checks

7.1 General

The concrete surfaces of the viaduct, including piers, abutments, crossheads, deck soffit and
parapet upstands, shall be inspected for defects at the frequencies given in Appendix C.
Inspection shall be carried out in good light conditions, and surfaces shall be cleared of
loose debris before examination where safe to do so.

The Marlowe Viaduct Maintenance Manual 2019 manual issue date is 2019-05-20. Record status: superseded.

7.2 Defects to Look For

| Defect | Typical Location | Action |
|--------|------------------|--------|
| Cracking (hairline, <0.3 mm) | Soffit, crossheads | Record location and width; monitor |
| Cracking (0.3–1.0 mm) | Piers, abutments | Record; arrange detailed survey |
| Cracking (>1.0 mm) | Any | Report immediately as category 1 |
| Spalling | Edges of crossheads, parapet | Record extent; arrange repair |
| Exposed reinforcement | Spalled areas | Report; arrange urgent repair |
| Efflorescence | Soffit, piers | Record; check for active water path |
| Staining / rust streaking | Around fixings, bearing shelves | Record; investigate source |
| Honeycombing | Cast-in-situ areas | Record; arrange assessment |

7.3 Crack Monitoring

Where cracks are to be monitored, a crack width gauge or tell-tale shall be fixed across the
crack. The position of each tell-tale shall be marked on a sketch and given a unique
reference. Readings shall be taken at six-monthly intervals and compared with the previous
readings. Any movement greater than 0.1 mm between readings shall be reported to the
Structures Manager.

7.4 Concrete Testing

In-situ concrete testing, such as carbonation depth testing or half-cell potential surveys,
shall only be carried out by specialist contractors. Results shall be appended to the
inspection record for the relevant element.

8. Drainage Maintenance

8.1 General

The drainage system of the viaduct comprises deck gullies, connecting pipes, downpipes and
outfalls to the watercourse. The system shall be kept free-flowing at all times. Blocked
gullies or pipes can lead to ponding on the deck and, in winter, to ice formation which
presents a hazard to road users.

8.2 Routine Maintenance
**Marlowe Viaduct Maintenance Manual 2019**

**8. Drainage Maintenance (continued)**

**8.3 Cleaning of Gullies and Downpipes**

Gullies shall be cleared of silt, leaves and other debris at intervals not exceeding six
months. Where the deck is subject to heavy tree cover or following a period of prolonged
leaf fall, additional cleaning visits shall be arranged as necessary.

Cleaning shall be carried out using a gully vacuum or by hand where access restrictions
apply. The operative shall record the date of cleaning, the gully reference, and any
observations of damage, blockages or missing gratings on the drainage inspection sheet
(Form D/2).

Downpipes shall be checked for blockages by rodding from the base. Where a blockage is
suspected but cannot be cleared by rodding, a CCTV survey of the affected section shall be
arranged. Any section of pipe found to be collapsed or severely deformed shall be reported
to the Structures Manager with a recommendation for repair or replacement.

**8.4 Outfalls and Watercourse**

The outfall structures to the watercourse shall be inspected at the same frequency as the
main structure inspection. The condition of the outfall headwall, any scour protection, and
the surrounding channel shall be noted. Accumulated debris at the outfall which may cause
backing up of the drainage system shall be removed.

Where the outfall discharges into a culvert, the condition of the culvert inlet and outlet
shall be examined. Any evidence of erosion or scour that threatens the stability of the
structure shall be reported immediately as a category 1 defect.

**9. Bearings and Movement Joints**

**9.1 General**

The viaduct is supported on laminated elastomeric bearings at the pier and abutment
positions. Movement joints are provided at each abutment and at the pier locations. The
correct function of bearings and joints is essential to the structural behaviour of the
viaduct. Their maintenance shall be given high priority.

**9.2 Bearing Inspection**

Bearings shall be examined during each principal inspection for:

- Splitting, cracking or delamination of the elastomer.
- Uneven compression or bulging of the elastomer.
- Displacement of the bearing relative to its seating.
- Corrosion of the sole plate, base plate or fixing bolts.
- Accumulation of debris or bird droppings around the bearing.

Where a bearing is found to be defective, the defect shall be recorded and the bearing
reference noted. Minor surface cracking of the elastomer may be monitored. Any bearing
showing signs of significant deformation or loss of section shall be reported to the
Structures Manager.

**9.3 Movement Joint Maintenance**

Movement joints shall be kept free of debris, particularly in the gutters and at the kerb
lines. The sealant in the joints shall be examined for loss of adhesion, splitting or
extrusion. Failed sealant shall be cut out and replaced with a suitable low-modulus sealant
in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.

The nosing material at the edges of the joint shall be checked for spalling or loss of
section. Where the joint is of the asphaltic plug type, the plug shall be inspected for
cracking, settlement or loss of fill. Repairs to asphaltic plug joints shall only be carried
out by a specialist contractor.

**10. Parapets, Barriers and Safety Fencing**

**10.1 General**

The parapets and safety barriers form part of the containment system for the viaduct. They
shall be maintained to ensure their structural adequacy and to prevent injury to the public
or damage to vehicles. Any damage that reduces the effectiveness of the containment system
shall be treated as a safety critical defect.
**Appendix A – Inspection Frequencies**

| Inspection Type | Frequency | Carried Out By | Record |
|-----------------|-----------|----------------|--------|
| Routine (walk-over) | 6 monthly | Term Maintenance Contractor | Form MW/R1 |
| General | 2 yearly | Structures Inspector | Form MW/G2 |
| Principal | 6 yearly | Structures Inspector (with access plant as required) | Form MW/P3 |
| Special / Post-event | As directed by Structures Manager | Structures Inspector or Engineer | Form MW/S4 |

Notes:

- The frequency of principal inspection is measured from the date of the previous principal
  inspection, not from the date of this manual.
- Where a defect is found that is judged to be safety critical, the Structures Manager shall be
  notified immediately and the frequency of subsequent inspections may be increased.
- Access requirements for each inspection type are given in Appendix C. Where access cannot be
  achieved safely, the inspection shall not proceed and the Structures Manager shall be advised
  so that alternative arrangements (e.g. lane closure, MEWP, underbridge unit) can be made.

**Appendix B – Defect Classification**

| Class | Description | Response |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| 1 | Safety critical – immediate danger to public or structure | Make safe immediately, notify Structures Manager |
| 2 | Significant – likely to become safety critical within 3 months | Repair within 1 month |
| 3 | Moderate – affecting durability or function | Repair within 6 months |
| 4 | Minor – no immediate effect | Monitor, repair at next routine opportunity |

Definitions:

- **Class 1** includes loss of containment, major spalling with risk of falling debris,
  significant bearing displacement, or severe scour.
- **Class 2** includes active corrosion with section loss, failed movement joint sealant with
  water ingress, or spalled concrete with exposed reinforcement.
- **Class 3** includes minor cracking, localised delamination, or blocked drainage outlets.
- **Class 4** includes surface staining, small hairline cracks, or minor fretting of edges.

The class assigned to a defect shall be reviewed at each subsequent inspection. Where the
condition changes, the class shall be amended on the inspection record and the appropriate
response timescale applied.

**Appendix C – Access Arrangements**

| Location | Access Method | Notes |
|----------|---------------|-------|
| Deck surface and parapets | From carriageway with traffic management | Full lane closure required for work at kerb line |
| Soffit of deck over carriageway | Underbridge unit or MEWP | Requires full closure of traffic beneath |
| Soffit of deck over water | Boat access or MEWP from river bank | Check river levels before deployment |
| Bearings at abutments | From access gallery at each abutment | Gallery lighting to be checked before entry |
| Bearings at piers | From access ladder and walkway | Harness and fall arrest required |
| Movement joints | From deck surface or underbridge unit | As required by joint type |

All access equipment shall be inspected and certified in accordance with current legislation
before use. The contractor shall provide a method statement and risk assessment for each access
arrangement prior to the start of any inspection or maintenance activity.

**Appendix D – Lubrication Schedule**

| Item | Lubricant | Frequency | Notes |
|------|-----------|-----------|-------|
| Bearing sliding surfaces (where accessible) | Molykote 111 or equivalent | 2 yearly | Do not over-apply; wipe off excess |
| Movement joint hinge pins | Lithium grease | Yearly | Only where grease nipples fitted |
| Access ladder hinges and locks | WD-40 or equivalent | Yearly | Check for corrosion before lubricating |
| Gallery door locks | Graphite powder | 2 yearly | Do not use oil-based lubricants on locks |

Source format: design specification

**2. Reference Documents**  
The following documents form part of this specification to the extent stated herein. Where there is a conflict, the requirements of this specification shall prevail.

- AEP-MV-DRG-201 to 215: General arrangement drawings for substructure and deck.  
- AEP-MV-CAL-007: Bearing load and movement calculations (Rev C).  
- AEP-MV-SPC-011: Concrete repair specification for plinth and shelf areas.  
- BS EN 1337-3: Structural bearings – Elastomeric bearings.  
- BS EN 1337-5: Structural bearings – Pot bearings.  
- BS EN 1991-2: Actions on structures – Traffic loads on bridges.  
- Highways England (now National Highways) BD 20/16 and BD 37/01 (as applicable).

**3. Definitions and Abbreviations**  
- MV: Marlowe Viaduct (also used as "MV" in site records and drawings).  
- Bearing: A structural device that transmits loads from the superstructure to the substructure while accommodating controlled movement and rotation.  
- Expansion joint: A device that accommodates movement between adjacent deck sections or between deck and abutment, while providing a continuous riding surface.  
- Plinth: The raised concrete pad on which a bearing is seated.  
- Muck away: Removal of excavated or surplus material from site.  
- Snagging: The process of identifying and rectifying minor defects prior to handover.

**4. Design Movement Capacity**

The design movement capacity for each bearing type is given in Table 4.1. The values represent the total design movement range (including creep, shrinkage, thermal effects, and traffic-induced deformation) that the bearing is required to accommodate over its design life. Movements are measured at the top of the bearing relative to the bottom, in the direction indicated.

**Table 4.1 – Design Movement Capacity (Current, Rev B)**

The design specification states that the Structural Bearing Type 7X design movement capacity is 45 mm. Record status: current. This value is the current controlled design basis and shall be used for all procurement, installation, and verification activities. No alternative movement capacity for Type 7X is accepted under this revision.

All Type 7X bearings shall be manufactured and tested to demonstrate compliance with the 45 mm longitudinal movement capacity. The testing shall be carried out in accordance with the procedure in Section 7 of this specification. The bearing shall be capable of achieving the full movement range without visible damage or permanent deformation.

The transverse movement capacity of 20 mm for Type 7X is applicable for skew effects and lateral temperature differentials. The vertical movement capacity of 5 mm is for local deck rotation and settlement effects. The rotation capacity of 0.015 radians is the maximum design rotation about any horizontal axis.

**5. Bearing Type 7X – Detailed Requirements**

5.1 General  
Type 7X bearings are elastomeric bearings with a steel-reinforced core, as detailed on drawing AEP-MV-DRG-204. The bearing shall be manufactured in accordance with BS EN 1337-3. The design life of the bearing is 50 years, subject to the inspection and maintenance regime defined in AEP-MV-SPC-021 (Maintenance Manual).

5.3 Dimensional Tolerances  
The following tolerances apply to Type 7X bearings:  
- Plan dimensions: ± 3 mm  
- Thickness: ± 2 mm  
- Flatness: 1 mm over the plan area  
- Edge cover: + 3 mm / - 0 mm

5.4 Load Ratings  
The design vertical load for Type 7X is 1,200 kN (characteristic) with a maximum service load of 950 kN. The design horizontal load is 150 kN. These values are for the worst-case load combination defined in AEP-MV-CAL-007.
6.4.1 Type A – Single Seal Joint  
Type A joints comprise a single elastomeric seal compressed between two steel edge profiles. The seal shall be a preformed, continuously vulcanised profile with a minimum shore hardness of 60 IRHD. The edge profiles shall be anchored to the deck concrete using chemical anchors or cast-in channels as detailed on AEP-MV-DRG-205. Type A joints are suitable for use at the abutments where the calculated longitudinal movement does not exceed 40 mm.

6.4.2 Type B – Asphaltic Plug Joint  
Type B joints are formed by a flexible asphaltic material placed in a prepared chase in the deck surfacing. The material shall be a polymer-modified bitumen with a softening point of not less than 90 °C. The chase dimensions shall be as detailed on AEP-MV-DRG-205. Type B joints are only permitted for minor remedial works and shall not be used on the main carriageway without the written approval of the Engineer.

6.4.3 Type C – Modular Joint  
Type C joints are modular joints comprising multiple seal elements supported on steel beams. The joint shall be designed to accommodate the full design movement range without overstressing the seal elements or the support structure. The seal elements shall be replaceable in service without the need to remove the entire joint. Type C joints are required at all locations where the calculated longitudinal movement exceeds 40 mm.

**Table 6.1 – Deck Expansion Joint Selection Schedule**

| Location | Joint Type | Design Movement (mm) | Drawing Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Abutment A1 | Type A | 32 | AEP-MV-DRG-205/01 |
| Abutment A2 | Type A | 35 | AEP-MV-DRG-205/02 |
| Pier P1 | Type C | 55 | AEP-MV-DRG-205/03 |
| Pier P2 | Type C | 62 | AEP-MV-DRG-205/04 |
| Pier P3 | Type C | 58 | AEP-MV-DRG-205/05 |

6.5 Type C – Modular Joint Detailed Requirements

6.5.1 General  
The design specification lists the Marlowe Viaduct deck expansion joint type as Modular 120. Record status: current. This designation shall be used for all Type C joints on the structure, regardless of the specific movement range at a particular pier. The Modular 120 system is a proprietary modular joint supplied by a specialist manufacturer and shall be installed strictly in accordance with the manufacturer's installation drawings and instructions.

6.5.2 Movement Capacity  
The Modular 120 joint shall be capable of accommodating a total longitudinal movement of 120 mm, comprising the calculated movement range plus an allowance for installation tolerances and long-term creep and shrinkage effects. The transverse movement capacity shall be 15 mm. The vertical differential movement across the joint shall not exceed 5 mm.

6.5.3 Seal Elements  
The joint shall comprise a minimum of three seal elements, each being a preformed EPDM profile with a service temperature range of -20 °C to +70 °C. The seal elements shall be held in place by extruded aluminium support bars. The support bars shall be bolted to the steel support beams using stainless steel fixings.

6.5.4 Support Beams  
The support beams shall be fabricated from S355 structural steel, hot-dip galvanised in accordance with BS EN ISO 1461. The beam section shall be designed to resist the wheel loads defined in BS EN 1991-2 without exceeding a deflection of span/600. The beams shall be supported on elastomeric bearing pads at each end, set into the deck concrete.

6.5.5 Edge Profiles  
The edge profiles at the interface between the joint and the deck surfacing shall be fabricated from steel angle, minimum 12 mm thick. The profiles shall be set flush with the finished road surface and shall be provided with a nosing detail to prevent the surfacing from breaking up at the joint edge.

6.5.
7.0 Installation Tolerances

7.1 General

Installation of all bearings and expansion joints shall be carried out in accordance with the tolerances set out in this Section and with the relevant drawings. Where a tighter tolerance is shown on a drawing or in the manufacturer's literature, the tighter tolerance shall apply. Any deviation beyond the tolerances given below shall be reported to the Engineer before proceeding, and a corrective method statement shall be submitted for approval.

7.2 Bearing Installation Tolerances

7.2.1 Bedding Mortar / Grout

The bearing shall be bedded on a proprietary structural grout having a minimum compressive strength of 60 N/mm² at 28 days. The grout bed shall be continuous and free from voids. The bearing sole plate shall be fully supported over its entire plan area.

7.2.2 Levelness

The upper surface of the bearing sole plate shall be level within 1 in 300 in any direction. The bearing top plate, after installation of the superstructure, shall be level within 1 in 300 unless a fall is specifically detailed on the drawings.

7.2.3 Plan Position

The centre of the bearing, as marked on the sole plate, shall be within ±5 mm of the setting-out position shown on the drawings. The longitudinal axis of the bearing shall be within ±0.5° of the line shown on the drawings.

7.2.4 Height / Line

The top of the bearing top plate shall be at the level shown on the drawings within ±3 mm, measured at the centre of the bearing. The difference in level between the top plates of bearings on the same pier or abutment shall not exceed 3 mm, unless otherwise noted.

7.2.5 Sliding Surfaces (PTFE / Stainless Steel)

Where a bearing incorporates a sliding surface, the sliding interface shall be clean and free from damage prior to installation. The stainless steel sliding surface shall be flat within 0.1 mm over any 300 mm length. The PTFE sheet shall be recessed into the mating plate such that the PTFE surface is below the surrounding plate level by 0.5 mm ± 0.2 mm.

7.3 Expansion Joint Installation Tolerances

7.3.1 Setting Gap

The gap setting at installation shall be as shown on the joint installation drawing or as instructed by the manufacturer. The setting gap shall be measured at the road surface level at each support line and shall be within ±5 mm of the specified value, unless a tighter tolerance is required for the particular joint type.

7.3.2 Levelness Across the Joint

The difference in level between the finished road surface on either side of the joint shall not exceed 3 mm. The joint itself shall not protrude above or be recessed below the adjacent finished surface by more than 2 mm. Localised deviations over a 3 m straightedge shall not exceed 3 mm.

7.3.3 Transverse Alignment

The joint shall be straight in plan, with a deviation of not more than 5 mm over a 3 m length, and not more than 10 mm over the full joint length.

7.3.4 Fixing Bolts / Dowels

All fixing bolts and dowels shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. Torque settings shall be as specified by the manufacturer and shall be checked with a calibrated torque wrench. The bolts shall be checked and re-tightened after the initial curing period of the surrounding concrete or grout.

7.3.5 Seal Installation

Preformed seals shall be installed without twisting or stretching. The seal shall be seated fully into the groove, and the top of the seal shall be flush with the adjacent surface within ±1 mm. The seal shall be continuous for the full length of the joint; site joints in seals shall only be made using the manufacturer's approved jointing method.

2. Inspection Regimes

2.1 General Inspection (GI)

A General Inspection shall be carried out at intervals not exceeding twelve months. The inspection shall be a visual examination of all parts of the structure that are readily accessible without special access equipment. The inspecting engineer shall record all defects, deterioration, and any changes from the previous inspection.

2.2 Principal Inspection (PI)

A Principal Inspection shall be carried out at intervals not exceeding six years. The PI shall involve close examination of all parts of the structure, including those requiring special access arrangements, such as the underside of the deck, the bearings, and the PT anchorages.

2.3 Special Inspections (SI)

Special Inspections shall be carried out following any exceptional event, including:
- Major flood events
- Vehicle impact on the structure or parapets
- Fire beneath or on the structure
- Seismic events (however minor)
- Any report of unusual vibration or movement

2.4 Inspection Schedule

| Inspection Type | Frequency | Responsible Party | Notes |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------------|-------|
| Routine visual | Monthly | HSA Area Crew | Drives over structure; check parapets, deck surface, drainage |
| GI | Annual | HSA Structures Team | Full visual from ground level and deck |
| PI | 6-yearly | HSA Structures Team / Specialist | Includes access units, PT inspection |
| SI | As required | HSA Structures Team | Triggered by events or findings |

In the Marlowe Viaduct Maintenance Manual 2019, the construction start date is recorded as 1968-04-15. Record status: historical.

3. Inspection Checklists

3.1 Monthly Routine Checklist

| Item | Check | Acceptance Criteria | Action if Failed |
|------|-------|---------------------|------------------|
| Deck surface | Potholes, rutting, debris | No defects > 20 mm deep | Arrange repair; clean deck |
| Expansion joints | Condition, debris, water tightness | Joints clear, no leakage | Clean or repair as required |
| Parapet/barriers | Impact damage, corrosion, loose fixings | No damage, fixings secure | Report to structures team |
| Drainage outlets | Blockage, standing water | Free-flowing | Clear blockage |
| Bearings (where visible) | Displacement, corrosion, debris | No visible distress | Report to structures team |
| Soffit (from ground) | Cracks, staining, spalling | No new or propagating cracks | Report to structures team |

3.2 General Inspection Checklist (Abridged)

| Item | Check | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| Deck | Cracking, spalling, delamination | Record on defect sheet |
| Parapets | Alignment, corrosion, fixings | Check all posts and rails |
| Bearings | Movement, corrosion, rubber condition | Record any anomalies |
| Piers/abutments | Cracks, leaching, vegetation | Check for settlement or scour |
| River protection | Scour, undermining | Record water level at time |
| Approach embankments | Erosion, settlement | Check for voids |

4. Maintenance Procedures

4.1 Concrete Repairs

4.1.1 Assessment

Before any concrete repair, the extent of the defect shall be assessed and recorded. Delaminated areas shall be identified by hammer tapping. The area shall be marked out and the extent of repair agreed with the structures team.

5. Lubrication Schedule

5.1 General

Lubrication shall be carried out in accordance with the intervals given below. All work shall be recorded on the Lubrication Record Sheet (Appendix B). Only lubricants specified by the bearing or equipment manufacturer shall be used. Where a grease nipple is missing or damaged, the item shall be reported and made good before the next lubrication visit.

The viaduct has three bearing types in service:

- Type A – Pot bearings (piers P2, P3, P4)
- Type B – Roller bearings (abutment A1)
- Type C – Elastomeric bearings (abutment A2, pier P1)

Note: Type B bearings at abutment A1 were replaced during the 2017 strengthening works. The original 1968 installation had a different lubrication point arrangement; refer to the as-built drawings for the current configuration.

5.2 Lubrication Intervals

The top and bottom plates shall be checked for distortion, and the anchorage bolts tested for
tightness using a torque wrench set to the values given on the as-built drawings. Where bolts
have been replaced, the replacement grade and torque shall be noted on the inspection record.

6.3 Roller Bearings (Type B)

Roller bearings at abutment A1 are of the multi-roller type. Free movement shall be confirmed
by observing the displacement of the bearing relative to the sole plate during a thermal
cycle, where practicable. The rollers shall be checked for pitting, rusting or flat spots.
Where any roller shows surface corrosion, the bearing shall be reported and a programme of
cleaning and re-greasing arranged.

Note: The replacement bearings installed in 2017 are fitted with a sealed cover plate.
Lubrication is via the two nipples on the side face. Do not attempt to open the cover plate
during routine inspection; this shall only be done during major works.

6.4 Elastomeric Bearings (Type C)

Elastomeric bearings at abutment A2 and pier P1 shall be visually checked for:

- Splitting or cracking of the rubber surface
- Bulging at the edges
- Uneven deformation suggesting overloading
- Displacement from the bearing shelf

Where bulging is observed, the bearing shall be checked for rebound after unloading. Any
permanent set shall be recorded and the bearing monitored at three-monthly intervals until
the next full structural assessment.

7. Concrete Checks

7.1 General

The concrete surfaces of the viaduct, including piers, abutments, crossheads, deck soffit and
parapet upstands, shall be inspected for defects at the frequencies given in Appendix C.
Inspection shall be carried out in good light conditions, and surfaces shall be cleared of
loose debris before examination where safe to do so.

The Marlowe Viaduct Maintenance Manual 2019 manual issue date is 2019-05-20. Record status: superseded.

7.2 Defects to Look For

| Defect | Typical Location | Action |
|--------|------------------|--------|
| Cracking (hairline, <0.3 mm) | Soffit, crossheads | Record location and width; monitor |
| Cracking (0.3–1.0 mm) | Piers, abutments | Record; arrange detailed survey |
| Cracking (>1.0 mm) | Any | Report immediately as category 1 |
| Spalling | Edges of crossheads, parapet | Record extent; arrange repair |
| Exposed reinforcement | Spalled areas | Report; arrange urgent repair |
| Efflorescence | Soffit, piers | Record; check for active water path |
| Staining / rust streaking | Around fixings, bearing shelves | Record; investigate source |
| Honeycombing | Cast-in-situ areas | Record; arrange assessment |

7.3 Crack Monitoring

Where cracks are to be monitored, a crack width gauge or tell-tale shall be fixed across the
crack. The position of each tell-tale shall be marked on a sketch and given a unique
reference. Readings shall be taken at six-monthly intervals and compared with the previous
readings. Any movement greater than 0.1 mm between readings shall be reported to the
Structures Manager.

7.4 Concrete Testing

In-situ concrete testing, such as carbonation depth testing or half-cell potential surveys,
shall only be carried out by specialist contractors. Results shall be appended to the
inspection record for the relevant element.

8. Drainage Maintenance

8.1 General

The drainage system of the viaduct comprises deck gullies, connecting pipes, downpipes and
outfalls to the watercourse. The system shall be kept free-flowing at all times. Blocked
gullies or pipes can lead to ponding on the deck and, in winter, to ice formation which
presents a hazard to road users.

8.2 Routine Maintenance

documents.title: Marlowe Viaduct Maintenance Manual 2019
documents.content:
**Marlowe Viaduct Maintenance Manual 2019**

**8. Drainage Maintenance (continued)**

**8.3 Cleaning of Gullies and Downpipes**

Gullies shall be cleared of silt, leaves and other debris at intervals not exceeding six
months. Where the deck is subject to heavy tree cover or following a period of prolonged
leaf fall, additional cleaning visits shall be arranged as necessary.

Cleaning shall be carried out using a gully vacuum or by hand where access restrictions
apply. The operative shall record the date of cleaning, the gully reference, and any
observations of damage, blockages or missing gratings on the drainage inspection sheet
(Form D/2).

Downpipes shall be checked for blockages by rodding from the base. Where a blockage is
suspected but cannot be cleared by rodding, a CCTV survey of the affected section shall be
arranged. Any section of pipe found to be collapsed or severely deformed shall be reported
to the Structures Manager with a recommendation for repair or replacement.

**8.4 Outfalls and Watercourse**

The outfall structures to the watercourse shall be inspected at the same frequency as the
main structure inspection. The condition of the outfall headwall, any scour protection, and
the surrounding channel shall be noted. Accumulated debris at the outfall which may cause
backing up of the drainage system shall be removed.

Where the outfall discharges into a culvert, the condition of the culvert inlet and outlet
shall be examined. Any evidence of erosion or scour that threatens the stability of the
structure shall be reported immediately as a category 1 defect.

**9. Bearings and Movement Joints**

**9.1 General**

The viaduct is supported on laminated elastomeric bearings at the pier and abutment
positions. Movement joints are provided at each abutment and at the pier locations. The
correct function of bearings and joints is essential to the structural behaviour of the
viaduct. Their maintenance shall be given high priority.

**9.2 Bearing Inspection**

Bearings shall be examined during each principal inspection for:

- Splitting, cracking or delamination of the elastomer.
- Uneven compression or bulging of the elastomer.
- Displacement of the bearing relative to its seating.
- Corrosion of the sole plate, base plate or fixing bolts.
- Accumulation of debris or bird droppings around the bearing.

Where a bearing is found to be defective, the defect shall be recorded and the bearing
reference noted. Minor surface cracking of the elastomer may be monitored. Any bearing
showing signs of significant deformation or loss of section shall be reported to the
Structures Manager.

**9.3 Movement Joint Maintenance**

Movement joints shall be kept free of debris, particularly in the gutters and at the kerb
lines. The sealant in the joints shall be examined for loss of adhesion, splitting or
extrusion. Failed sealant shall be cut out and replaced with a suitable low-modulus sealant
in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.

The nosing material at the edges of the joint shall be checked for spalling or loss of
section. Where the joint is of the asphaltic plug type, the plug shall be inspected for
cracking, settlement or loss of fill. Repairs to asphaltic plug joints shall only be carried
out by a specialist contractor.

**10. Parapets, Barriers and Safety Fencing**

**10.1 General**

The parapets and safety barriers form part of the containment system for the viaduct. They
shall be maintained to ensure their structural adequacy and to prevent injury to the public
or damage to vehicles. Any damage that reduces the effectiveness of the containment system
shall be treated as a safety critical defect.

**Appendix A – Inspection Frequencies**

| Inspection Type | Frequency | Carried Out By | Record |
|-----------------|-----------|----------------|--------|
| Routine (walk-over) | 6 monthly | Term Maintenance Contractor | Form MW/R1 |
| General | 2 yearly | Structures Inspector | Form MW/G2 |
| Principal | 6 yearly | Structures Inspector (with access plant as required) | Form MW/P3 |
| Special / Post-event | As directed by Structures Manager | Structures Inspector or Engineer | Form MW/S4 |

Notes:

- The frequency of principal inspection is measured from the date of the previous principal
  inspection, not from the date of this manual.
- Where a defect is found that is judged to be safety critical, the Structures Manager shall be
  notified immediately and the frequency of subsequent inspections may be increased.
- Access requirements for each inspection type are given in Appendix C. Where access cannot be
  achieved safely, the inspection shall not proceed and the Structures Manager shall be advised
  so that alternative arrangements (e.g. lane closure, MEWP, underbridge unit) can be made.

**Appendix B – Defect Classification**

| Class | Description | Response |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| 1 | Safety critical – immediate danger to public or structure | Make safe immediately, notify Structures Manager |
| 2 | Significant – likely to become safety critical within 3 months | Repair within 1 month |
| 3 | Moderate – affecting durability or function | Repair within 6 months |
| 4 | Minor – no immediate effect | Monitor, repair at next routine opportunity |

Definitions:

- **Class 1** includes loss of containment, major spalling with risk of falling debris,
  significant bearing displacement, or severe scour.
- **Class 2** includes active corrosion with section loss, failed movement joint sealant with
  water ingress, or spalled concrete with exposed reinforcement.
- **Class 3** includes minor cracking, localised delamination, or blocked drainage outlets.
- **Class 4** includes surface staining, small hairline cracks, or minor fretting of edges.

The class assigned to a defect shall be reviewed at each subsequent inspection. Where the
condition changes, the class shall be amended on the inspection record and the appropriate
response timescale applied.

**Appendix C – Access Arrangements**

| Location | Access Method | Notes |
|----------|---------------|-------|
| Deck surface and parapets | From carriageway with traffic management | Full lane closure required for work at kerb line |
| Soffit of deck over carriageway | Underbridge unit or MEWP | Requires full closure of traffic beneath |
| Soffit of deck over water | Boat access or MEWP from river bank | Check river levels before deployment |
| Bearings at abutments | From access gallery at each abutment | Gallery lighting to be checked before entry |
| Bearings at piers | From access ladder and walkway | Harness and fall arrest required |
| Movement joints | From deck surface or underbridge unit | As required by joint type |

All access equipment shall be inspected and certified in accordance with current legislation
before use. The contractor shall provide a method statement and risk assessment for each access
arrangement prior to the start of any inspection or maintenance activity.

**Appendix D – Lubrication Schedule**

| Item | Lubricant | Frequency | Notes |
|------|-----------|-----------|-------|
| Bearing sliding surfaces (where accessible) | Molykote 111 or equivalent | 2 yearly | Do not over-apply; wipe off excess |
| Movement joint hinge pins | Lithium grease | Yearly | Only where grease nipples fitted |
| Access ladder hinges and locks | WD-40 or equivalent | Yearly | Check for corrosion before lubricating |
| Gallery door locks | Graphite powder | 2 yearly | Do not use oil-based lubricants on locks |

documents.content:
**2. Reference Documents**  
The following documents form part of this specification to the extent stated herein. Where there is a conflict, the requirements of this specification shall prevail.

- AEP-MV-DRG-201 to 215: General arrangement drawings for substructure and deck.  
- AEP-MV-CAL-007: Bearing load and movement calculations (Rev C).  
- AEP-MV-SPC-011: Concrete repair specification for plinth and shelf areas.  
- BS EN 1337-3: Structural bearings – Elastomeric bearings.  
- BS EN 1337-5: Structural bearings – Pot bearings.  
- BS EN 1991-2: Actions on structures – Traffic loads on bridges.  
- Highways England (now National Highways) BD 20/16 and BD 37/01 (as applicable).

**3. Definitions and Abbreviations**  
- MV: Marlowe Viaduct (also used as "MV" in site records and drawings).  
- Bearing: A structural device that transmits loads from the superstructure to the substructure while accommodating controlled movement and rotation.  
- Expansion joint: A device that accommodates movement between adjacent deck sections or between deck and abutment, while providing a continuous riding surface.  
- Plinth: The raised concrete pad on which a bearing is seated.  
- Muck away: Removal of excavated or surplus material from site.  
- Snagging: The process of identifying and rectifying minor defects prior to handover.

**4. Design Movement Capacity**

The design movement capacity for each bearing type is given in Table 4.1. The values represent the total design movement range (including creep, shrinkage, thermal effects, and traffic-induced deformation) that the bearing is required to accommodate over its design life. Movements are measured at the top of the bearing relative to the bottom, in the direction indicated.

**Table 4.1 – Design Movement Capacity (Current, Rev B)**

The design specification states that the Structural Bearing Type 7X design movement capacity is 45 mm. Record status: current. This value is the current controlled design basis and shall be used for all procurement, installation, and verification activities. No alternative movement capacity for Type 7X is accepted under this revision.

All Type 7X bearings shall be manufactured and tested to demonstrate compliance with the 45 mm longitudinal movement capacity. The testing shall be carried out in accordance with the procedure in Section 7 of this specification. The bearing shall be capable of achieving the full movement range without visible damage or permanent deformation.

The transverse movement capacity of 20 mm for Type 7X is applicable for skew effects and lateral temperature differentials. The vertical movement capacity of 5 mm is for local deck rotation and settlement effects. The rotation capacity of 0.015 radians is the maximum design rotation about any horizontal axis.

**5. Bearing Type 7X – Detailed Requirements**

5.1 General  
Type 7X bearings are elastomeric bearings with a steel-reinforced core, as detailed on drawing AEP-MV-DRG-204. The bearing shall be manufactured in accordance with BS EN 1337-3. The design life of the bearing is 50 years, subject to the inspection and maintenance regime defined in AEP-MV-SPC-021 (Maintenance Manual).

5.3 Dimensional Tolerances  
The following tolerances apply to Type 7X bearings:  
- Plan dimensions: ± 3 mm  
- Thickness: ± 2 mm  
- Flatness: 1 mm over the plan area  
- Edge cover: + 3 mm / - 0 mm

5.4 Load Ratings  
The design vertical load for Type 7X is 1,200 kN (characteristic) with a maximum service load of 950 kN. The design horizontal load is 150 kN. These values are for the worst-case load combination defined in AEP-MV-CAL-007.

6.4.1 Type A – Single Seal Joint  
Type A joints comprise a single elastomeric seal compressed between two steel edge profiles. The seal shall be a preformed, continuously vulcanised profile with a minimum shore hardness of 60 IRHD. The edge profiles shall be anchored to the deck concrete using chemical anchors or cast-in channels as detailed on AEP-MV-DRG-205. Type A joints are suitable for use at the abutments where the calculated longitudinal movement does not exceed 40 mm.

6.4.2 Type B – Asphaltic Plug Joint  
Type B joints are formed by a flexible asphaltic material placed in a prepared chase in the deck surfacing. The material shall be a polymer-modified bitumen with a softening point of not less than 90 °C. The chase dimensions shall be as detailed on AEP-MV-DRG-205. Type B joints are only permitted for minor remedial works and shall not be used on the main carriageway without the written approval of the Engineer.

6.4.3 Type C – Modular Joint  
Type C joints are modular joints comprising multiple seal elements supported on steel beams. The joint shall be designed to accommodate the full design movement range without overstressing the seal elements or the support structure. The seal elements shall be replaceable in service without the need to remove the entire joint. Type C joints are required at all locations where the calculated longitudinal movement exceeds 40 mm.

6.5 Type C – Modular Joint Detailed Requirements

6.5.1 General  
The design specification lists the Marlowe Viaduct deck expansion joint type as Modular 120. Record status: current. This designation shall be used for all Type C joints on the structure, regardless of the specific movement range at a particular pier. The Modular 120 system is a proprietary modular joint supplied by a specialist manufacturer and shall be installed strictly in accordance with the manufacturer's installation drawings and instructions.

6.5.2 Movement Capacity  
The Modular 120 joint shall be capable of accommodating a total longitudinal movement of 120 mm, comprising the calculated movement range plus an allowance for installation tolerances and long-term creep and shrinkage effects. The transverse movement capacity shall be 15 mm. The vertical differential movement across the joint shall not exceed 5 mm.

6.5.3 Seal Elements  
The joint shall comprise a minimum of three seal elements, each being a preformed EPDM profile with a service temperature range of -20 °C to +70 °C. The seal elements shall be held in place by extruded aluminium support bars. The support bars shall be bolted to the steel support beams using stainless steel fixings.

6.5.4 Support Beams  
The support beams shall be fabricated from S355 structural steel, hot-dip galvanised in accordance with BS EN ISO 1461. The beam section shall be designed to resist the wheel loads defined in BS EN 1991-2 without exceeding a deflection of span/600. The beams shall be supported on elastomeric bearing pads at each end, set into the deck concrete.

6.5.5 Edge Profiles  
The edge profiles at the interface between the joint and the deck surfacing shall be fabricated from steel angle, minimum 12 mm thick. The profiles shall be set flush with the finished road surface and shall be provided with a nosing detail to prevent the surfacing from breaking up at the joint edge.

7.0 Installation Tolerances

7.1 General

Installation of all bearings and expansion joints shall be carried out in accordance with the tolerances set out in this Section and with the relevant drawings. Where a tighter tolerance is shown on a drawing or in the manufacturer's literature, the tighter tolerance shall apply. Any deviation beyond the tolerances given below shall be reported to the Engineer before proceeding, and a corrective method statement shall be submitted for approval.

7.2 Bearing Installation Tolerances

7.2.1 Bedding Mortar / Grout

The bearing shall be bedded on a proprietary structural grout having a minimum compressive strength of 60 N/mm² at 28 days. The grout bed shall be continuous and free from voids. The bearing sole plate shall be fully supported over its entire plan area.

7.2.2 Levelness

The upper surface of the bearing sole plate shall be level within 1 in 300 in any direction. The bearing top plate, after installation of the superstructure, shall be level within 1 in 300 unless a fall is specifically detailed on the drawings.

7.2.3 Plan Position

The centre of the bearing, as marked on the sole plate, shall be within ±5 mm of the setting-out position shown on the drawings. The longitudinal axis of the bearing shall be within ±0.5° of the line shown on the drawings.

7.2.4 Height / Line

The top of the bearing top plate shall be at the level shown on the drawings within ±3 mm, measured at the centre of the bearing. The difference in level between the top plates of bearings on the same pier or abutment shall not exceed 3 mm, unless otherwise noted.

7.2.5 Sliding Surfaces (PTFE / Stainless Steel)

Where a bearing incorporates a sliding surface, the sliding interface shall be clean and free from damage prior to installation. The stainless steel sliding surface shall be flat within 0.1 mm over any 300 mm length. The PTFE sheet shall be recessed into the mating plate such that the PTFE surface is below the surrounding plate level by 0.5 mm ± 0.2 mm.

7.3 Expansion Joint Installation Tolerances

7.3.1 Setting Gap

The gap setting at installation shall be as shown on the joint installation drawing or as instructed by the manufacturer. The setting gap shall be measured at the road surface level at each support line and shall be within ±5 mm of the specified value, unless a tighter tolerance is required for the particular joint type.

7.3.2 Levelness Across the Joint

The difference in level between the finished road surface on either side of the joint shall not exceed 3 mm. The joint itself shall not protrude above or be recessed below the adjacent finished surface by more than 2 mm. Localised deviations over a 3 m straightedge shall not exceed 3 mm.

7.3.3 Transverse Alignment

The joint shall be straight in plan, with a deviation of not more than 5 mm over a 3 m length, and not more than 10 mm over the full joint length.

7.3.4 Fixing Bolts / Dowels

All fixing bolts and dowels shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. Torque settings shall be as specified by the manufacturer and shall be checked with a calibrated torque wrench. The bolts shall be checked and re-tightened after the initial curing period of the surrounding concrete or grout.

7.3.5 Seal Installation

Preformed seals shall be installed without twisting or stretching. The seal shall be seated fully into the groove, and the top of the seal shall be flush with the adjacent surface within ±1 mm. The seal shall be continuous for the full length of the joint; site joints in seals shall only be made using the manufacturer's approved jointing method.
